$schema: Material catalog for Printer Tycoon. Costs reflect typical 2024-2026 retail USD; use wholesale tier discounts as a progression mechanic. Difficulty 1 (easy) to 5 (specialist). Refresh annually.

fields.tech: FDM | MSLA | SLA | SLS | MJF | DMLS | ADAM | FFF
fields.costPerKg: USD per kilogram for filaments and powders; null otherwise
fields.costPerLiter: USD per liter for resins; null otherwise
fields.printTempC: [min, max] hot end / laser nominal range
fields.bedTempC: [min, max] heated bed range; null if N/A
fields.needsEnclosure: true if printer must be enclosed/heated chamber for reliable results
fields.needsHardenedNozzle: true if abrasive — soft brass nozzle wears out fast
fields.needsDryer: true if hygroscopic — must be dried before printing
fields.stringFactor: 0..1, contribution to surface defects affecting quality score
fields.strengthMPa: tensile strength, used for engineering-order matching
fields.flexShoreA: Shore A hardness for flexibles (null if rigid)
fields.foodSafe: true if food-contact safe (with proper finish)
fields.biocompatible: true if cleared for skin contact / dental / medical
fields.valueMultiplier: rough sell-price multiplier vs PLA baseline (1.0)

materials.name: PLA
materials.notes: The default. Biodegradable corn-based plastic. Easy to print on anything, but soft in a hot car. Most consumer prints (toys, decor, prototypes) are PLA.

materials.name: PLA+ / Tough PLA
materials.notes: PLA with toughness modifiers. Better impact resistance, slightly less brittle. Same printability.

materials.name: PETG
materials.notes: Tougher than PLA, food-safe, mild UV resistance. Strings if not retraction-tuned. Hygroscopic — leaves a wet hiss if not dried.

materials.name: TPU 95A
materials.notes: Flexible filament. Phone cases, gaskets, shoe parts. Slow print speeds (30-50 mm/s) and direct-drive extruder strongly recommended.

materials.name: ABS
materials.notes: LEGO plastic. Tough, machinable, acetone-smoothable. Warps badly without an enclosure. Releases styrene fumes — needs ventilation.

materials.name: ASA
materials.notes: ABS's outdoor-rated cousin. Survives sun, rain, freezing. Same print difficulty as ABS but commands a premium for automotive and outdoor parts.

materials.name: Polycarbonate (PC)
materials.notes: Bulletproof-glass material. Extremely strong, transparent variants. Very hot bed and chamber required. Aggressive warping without enclosure.

materials.name: Nylon (PA12)
materials.notes: Engineering nylon. Excellent abrasion resistance, slight flex, low friction. Aggressively absorbs moisture — must dry before every print.

materials.name: PA-CF (Carbon Fiber Nylon)
materials.notes: Chopped carbon fiber in nylon matrix. Stiff, dimensionally stable, looks pro. Wears soft brass nozzles in 100 hours — hardened steel or ruby required.

materials.name: PEEK
materials.notes: Aerospace-grade thermoplastic. Withstands continuous 250C, autoclavable, biocompatible. Requires 380C+ hot end and 90C+ heated chamber. Niche but premium-priced.

materials.name: Standard Resin
materials.notes: Generic photopolymer. Excellent surface finish, brittle. Toxic uncured — gloves and ventilation required. Yellows in sunlight.

materials.name: Tough Resin (ABS-like)
materials.notes: Impact-resistant resin for functional prototypes. Less brittle than standard. Slightly longer cure time.

materials.name: Flexible Resin
materials.notes: Rubber-like resin. Wearables, gaskets, soft-touch grips. Demanding supports — overhangs sag during cure.

materials.name: Castable Resin
materials.notes: Burns out clean in lost-wax casting. The jewelry workflow: print master, invest in plaster, burn out, pour metal. High margin for ring/pendant work.

materials.name: Engineering Resin (Tough 2000)
materials.notes: Formlabs-style engineering resin: stiff, durable, dimensionally stable. Functional prototypes, jigs and fixtures, end-use small parts.
